packages.deviations:
Two intentional, both grounded in the existing codebase and noted inline as comments in the tests:

1. T4's plan text writes a fixture payment as `status: "CONFIRMED"`, but PaymentStatus (finance.prisma) only has DRAFT|PAID|VOID, and this codebase's own convention (payment-predicates.ts's `CONFIRMED_PAYMENT = { status: "PAID" }`, comments everywhere say "CONFIRMED (PAID)") makes "PAID" the real enum value for the CONFIRMED basis. I used `status: "PAID"` in the fixture — using the literal "CONFIRMED" would make the test wrong under any correct implementation (no row would ever satisfy it).

2. T5 harness note mentions extending "statement-apply.service.spec.ts if it has a harness" — no such file exists (the actual sibling spec is named `statement-apply.spec.ts`, not in my allowed-to-write list), so T5's behavioral (mocked-data) coverage lives only in supplier-statements.service.spec.ts via the public `scanStatement` → `matchAgainstBills` → `fetchMatchableBills` path. statement-apply.service.ts's own byte-copied query is covered structurally (not behaviorally) by T5-guard, which scans both files' source text for `take: 500`, a private `vendorBill.findMany`, and the required `fetchMatchableBills` import from `./matchable-bills`.

Also flagging (not a deviation, just uncertainty): T6's `where.status.notIn` assertion in getKpiSummary is my best-grounded inference from the codebase's own `notIn` idiom (invoices.service.ts ~line 5672) and the page.tsx exclusion list (PAID/VOID/WRITTEN_OFF/DRAFT) — invoice-status-sets.ts doesn't yet define a named OPEN set (that's the build phase's job), so the exact Prisma shape wasn't specified by the plan. The numeric KPI assertions (`toEqual` on the full result object) are the load-bearing oracle regardless of that shape.

apps/web/app/(dashboard)/orders/orders-page.test.tsx was NOT created. T9 is conditional in the test plan ("only if an RTL harness precedent for a list page exists; else skip and say so"). I searched the repo (`grep -rl "useOrders\|useInvoices\b" apps/web --include="*.test.tsx"`) and found zero existing RTL tests for any list page (orders/invoices/customers) that mock a list hook and assert on pager/search behavior — the only precedents are detail-page tests (bookkeeping/[transactionId]/page.test.tsx, settings tabs). Before this change both halves of the wallet came from ONE read: `creditNote.findMany({ where: { customerId }, orderBy: createdAt desc, take: 50 })`. `availableCredit` summed that 50-row page and `transactions` listed the same 50 rows, so the dollar value and the credit rows always agreed (both wrong the same way — that is B110).

After this change they are two different populations:
- `openCreditNotes` (line 976-979 area, `where: { customerId, status: { not: "VOID" } }`, NO take) -> `availableCredit` at line 1034.
- `ledgerCreditNotesRaw` (`take: LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP + 1` = 51, `orderBy: createdAt desc`, line 979) -> `ledgerCreditNotes` (line 1009) -> the `transactions` array.

Three existing consumers read the credits out of `transactions`, not out of `availableCredit`:
- apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/finances/page.tsx:106-108 — `activeCredits = (statement?.transactions ?? []).filter(t => t.type === "CREDIT_NOTE" && t.runningBalance > 0.001).slice(0,6)`; rendered as the tile sub-label at :182 (`${activeCredits.length} active` / "None available") and as the credit LIST at :219-226.
- apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/payments/page.tsx:145-147 and :254 — same derivation, same sub-label.
- apps/mobile/app/(customer)/payments.tsx:66 — `activeCreditRows(statement?.transactions)`.

Failure scenario: a buyer has 60 credit notes. The 50 newest are fully consumed (`amount - amountUsed == 0`); ten older ones still hold $50 each. After this change `availableCredit` = $500 (uncapped read sees the ten old ones), while `transactions` holds only the newest 50 credit notes, every one of which has `runningBalance` 0. The web buyer portal then renders the wallet tile as "$500.00" with the sub-label "None available", and the `activeCredits.length > 0 &&` guard at finances/page.tsx:219 suppresses the credit list entirely — the buyer is told they hold $500 of store credit and simultaneously that they have none, with no row to identify. The mobile screen behaves the same way. The `transactionsTruncated` flag that this change added exactly to disclose a capped ledger is wired only into the OPERATOR surfaces (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx LedgerTruncationNote, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/customers/[id]/statement.tsx); the buyer surfaces got the field in their types (packages/types/api/buyer.ts `BuyerStatement.transactionsTruncated`) but no consumer.

The new code comment at customers.service.ts:966-971 asserts "the LEDGER caps below are for the transactions DISPLAY only — the money figures ... are computed from the separate, uncapped OPEN-set reads". That invariant is false across the package boundary: three call sites derive a money-bearing list (which credits the buyer can spend) from the capped array.
findings.fixHint: Either return the open credit-note rows as their own field on the statement (e.g. `activeCredits`) and repoint finances/page.tsx:106, payments/page.tsx:145 and mobile payments.tsx:66 at it, or keep the credit-note ledger read uncapped so the list and `availableCredit` stay one population. If neither, wire `transactionsTruncated` into the buyer surfaces so the count is at least labelled partial.
findings.decision: The evidence shows a real split: availableCredit now sums an uncapped non-VOID read while the buyer-facing credit rows and their count still come from the 51-row ledger page, and nothing labels the ledger as partial (the truncation flag has no consumer and its predicate is already flagged wrong). It is a visible tile-vs-rows contradiction on a buyer surface, but it is a consequence of the accepted uncapped-totals/capped-ledger design rather than a wrong dollar figure, so minor and largely absorbed by the open no-consumer/wrong-predicate findings.

findings.summary: The customer Statement tab's four-tile header now mixes bases: "Invoiced Amount" and "Amount Received" are still summed from the 100-row capped `transactions` ledger while "Balance Due" was repointed at the newly uncapped, DRAFT-excluding `outstandingAmount`, so the three tiles no longer reconcile.
findings.detail:
The tiles are built at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx:3818-3863:
- :3828 "Invoiced Amount" = `statement.transactions.filter(tx => tx.type === "INVOICE").reduce((s,tx) => s + Math.abs(tx.amount), 0)`
- :3839 "Amount Received" = that figure minus `Σ |tx.runningBalance|` over the same INVOICE rows (the comment says explicitly "received = invoiced − still-owed on the listed rows")
- :3854 "Balance Due" = `statement?.outstandingAmount`

Before this change all three came from ONE population: `invoice.findMany({ where: { customerId }, orderBy: createdAt desc, take: 100 })` — `outstandingAmount` was reduced from exactly the rows that became `transactions`, so `Invoiced − Received = Balance Due` held by construction over those 100 rows.

After this change (apps/api/src/customers/customers.service.ts:955-1030) `outstandingAmount` comes from `openInvoices` — an uncapped read with `status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED }` (PAID/VOID/WRITTEN_OFF/DRAFT excluded) — while `transactions` is still built from `ledgerInvoices`, the newest 100 rows of ALL statuses.

Failure scenario: a customer with 250 invoices of which 120 are open, totalling $60,000 outstanding; the 100 newest invoices total $40,000 invoiced with $30,000 still owed on them. The Statement tab now renders Opening Balance $0.00 / Invoiced Amount $40,000.00 / Amount Received $10,000.00 / Balance Due $60,000.00 — arithmetic an operator (or the customer they print this statement for) cannot reconcile: 0 + 40,000 − 10,000 = 30,000, not 60,000. Two further axes push the same way: the ledger includes DRAFT invoices (so "Invoiced Amount" counts totals "Balance Due" deliberately excludes), and `runningBalance` per row switched to the CONFIRMED (`sumConfirmed`) basis while nothing else in the tile row did.

The `LedgerTruncationNote` added at :3873 sits BELOW this tile row and says only that the transaction LIST is partial; it does not tell the reader that three of the four numbers above it are computed from that partial list while the fourth is not.
findings.fixHint: Feed the tile row from the same population as Balance Due — either have the API return invoiced/received totals alongside `outstandingAmount` (computed over the same uncapped open set), or move the truncation note above the tile row and label the two ledger-derived tiles as covering the listed transactions only.
findings.decision: Before the change the three Statement-tab tiles were reduced from one 100-row population so Invoiced − Received = Balance Due held by construction; now Balance Due is the uncapped DRAFT-excluding outstandingAmount while the other two are still summed off the capped ledger rows, so an operator sees three money tiles that no longer add up. That is a new, user-visible arithmetic contradiction introduced by this change on a money screen.

findings.summary: The customer Invoices-tab summary bar now mixes a whole-tenant figure with two chip-scoped ones: "Outstanding" reads the statement while "Overdue" and "Total Invoices" are still counted off the currently-filtered, 50-row `invoicesData` page.
findings.detail:
apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx:3531-3568. `invoicesData` is `useInvoices({ customerId, status: invoiceFilter === "paid" ? "PAID" : invoiceFilter === "void" ? "VOID" : undefined, limit: 50 })` (declared at :1957-1961) — it re-fetches whenever the operator clicks the All / Outstanding / Paid / Void chips at :3583-3600. `overdueCount` (:3539) and "Total Invoices" (:3568, `invoicesData?.meta?.total`) therefore track the active chip, while `outstandingTotal` (:3540) is now `statement?.outstandingAmount`, which never varies with the chip.

Before this change all three cards were derived from the same `invoicesData` response, so they moved together.

Failure scenario: a customer with $12,400 open and 3 VOID invoices. The operator clicks the "Void" chip. The card row then reads "Outstanding $12,400.00 · Overdue 0 invoices · Total Invoices 3" — the header claims the customer has three invoices while showing the full open balance beside it. The "Paid" chip produces the same shape.

Secondary: `statement` is a separate query (`useCustomerStatement`, :1949) with no loading state consumed here, so while it is in flight the Outstanding card renders `$0.00` in success styling (`text-success`, :3546) rather than a skeleton — previously it was derived from data the tab had already loaded.
findings.fixHint: Either scope the whole card row to the statement (drive Overdue/Total from server-side figures too) or leave a chip-independent label on the Outstanding card so it does not read as a property of the filtered set.
findings.decision: The Outstanding card was repointed at the statement (whole-customer, chip-independent) while Overdue and Total Invoices still track the active status chip and the 50-row page, so the Void chip can read 'Outstanding $12,400 · Total Invoices 3'. A real mixed-scope header, but a labelling inconsistency rather than a wrong amount.

findings.summary: The orders CSV export was rewritten to send its filters to the server instead of filtering client-side, but `productId` — a filter that IS applied to the on-screen list — was not added to the export params, so exporting with a product chip active produces a CSV of every order.
findings.detail:
The B144 fix's stated purpose is that a filter must reach the server rather than be applied to whatever page the client happens to hold. The on-screen query at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/orders/page.tsx:341-350 sends `status`, `urgent`, `deliveryDateFrom`, `deliveryDateTo`, `productId: productIdFilter || undefined`, `fulfillPath`, `search`, `page`, `limit`. `handleExport` (:373-400) sends `status`, `urgent`, `deliveryDateFrom`, `deliveryDateTo`, `fulfillPath`, `search`, `page: 1`, `limit: 1000` — no `productId`. This hunk was edited by this change (the `search` line at :397 was added and the client-side `.filter()` over `payload.data` was deleted), so the param list was under the author's hand. Failure scenario: the operator opens `/orders?productId=

` (the "which orders had this item?" chip, whose label is rendered from `useProduct(productIdFilter)` at :147), sees 12 matching orders, clicks Export. The request goes out without `productId`, the API returns the first 1000 orders for the tenant, and `downloadCsv` writes all of them — the CSV silently contains orders that do not contain the product, and previously the deleted client-side filter did not catch this either (it only matched on business name / order number). The operator's on-screen count and their CSV row count disagree by three orders of magnitude. Separately, `EXPORT_LIMIT = 1000` is now exactly `MAX_LIST_LIMIT`, so with `@Max(MAX_LIST_LIMIT)` newly added to `ListOrdersDto.limit` (apps/api/src/orders/dto/list-orders.dto.ts:28) the export can no longer be widened past 1000 without a DTO change, and a tenant with more than 1000 matching orders gets a silently truncated CSV with no warning — the same silent-truncation class F16 exists to remove.
findings.fixHint: Add `productId: productIdFilter || undefined` to the handleExport params so the export matches the on-screen query exactly.
findings.decision: The B144 hunk was rewritten so export filters travel to the server, yet productId — which the on-screen query does send — was left out of the export params, so a product-filtered view exports every order. The evidence does not prove the deleted client-side filter previously honoured productId, so it may be pre-existing, but it is in the edited hunk and squarely within the bug's stated purpose.

findings.summary: `getKpiSummary` buckets purely by due date and drops the client memo's `status === "OVERDUE"` disjunct, but the Overdue tile it feeds still filters the list by `status=OVERDUE` on click, so the tile's value and the list it opens can disagree.
findings.detail:
Server bucketing: apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3050-3055 — `if (dueDateIso == null) continue; if (dueDateIso < today) overdue += balance; else if (dueDateIso === today) dueToday += balance; else if (dueDateIso <= cutoff) dueIn30 += balance;`. The memo this replaces (deleted at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:225-320) read `if (inv.status === "OVERDUE" || (due && due < today && openForCollection)) overdue += balance;` — status OR date.

The tile is still a filter button: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:284-291 renders `label: "Overdue", value: fmt(kpis.overdue)` with `onClick: () => onFilter(activeFilter === "OVERDUE" ? "" : "OVERDUE")`, which sets `statusFilter` and is sent to `findAll` as `status`, matching the literal `InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE` column (invoices.service.ts:2820-2821).

The divergent state is reachable: `update(id, dto)` at apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3156 writes `...(dto.dueDate && { dueDate: new Date(dto.dueDate) })` (:3360) and never calls `recomputeStatus` — unlike `updateInvoiceTerms`, which does (:~3480, `const newStatus = this.recomputeStatus(totalPaid, Number(inv.total), newDueDate, inv.status)`). So an invoice already stamped OVERDUE by the nightly job, whose due date is then pushed forward through the generic invoice update, keeps `status = OVERDUE` with a future `dueDate`.

Failure scenario: INV-1, balance $5,000, status OVERDUE, dueDate moved to today+10 via a plain invoice edit; it is the tenant's only past-due row. The Overdue tile now shows $0.00 (INV-1 is bucketed into dueIn30 instead); the operator clicks it and the list returns INV-1 with $5,000 due. The behaviour is deliberately pinned by the new T6 case `inv-status-overdue`, so the test suite will not surface it — the defect is that the pinned semantics break the tile's own click target.
findings.fixHint: Either restore the `status === OVERDUE` disjunct in the server bucketing, or change the Overdue tile's onClick to the derived `isOverdue` filter that findAll already implements (status in SENT/VIEWED/PARTIAL/OVERDUE and dueDate < now) so value and filter share one definition.
findings.decision: The server buckets Overdue by dueDate only while the tile's click still filters the list by status=OVERDUE, and the evidence shows the status/date divergence is reachable via update(); the tile value and the list it opens can disagree. Kept as minor because the date-only bucketing may be the cause-ruling's chosen definition — the fixer must check section 2 before treating it as a defect rather than re-adding the disjunct.

findings.summary: `getKpiSummary` replaces a 999-row client cap with an unbounded server `findMany` that materializes every open invoice plus every one of their payment rows in Node on each `/invoices` load, while the sibling figure in the same `Promise.all` is a proper SQL aggregate.
findings.detail:
apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3001-3009: `this.prisma.forTenant().invoice.findMany({ where: { status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED }, ...(customerId ? { customerId } : {}) }, select: { total: true, dueDate: true, payments: { select: { amount: true, status: true } } } })` — no `take`, no pagination, and a nested relation select so Prisma issues a second query with an `IN (...)` list of every open invoice id. The five money figures are then reduced in JS at :3044-3056.

The `avgDays` leg of the same `Promise.all` (:3013-3027) is a single `$queryRaw` `AVG(...)` — so the aggregate-in-SQL option was available and used for one of the six tiles and not the other five.

Failure scenario: an established tenant carrying 40,000 open invoices with an average of 2 payment rows each. Every operator opening `/invoices` (and every React Query refetch after any invoice mutation invalidates the `["invoices"]` key) pulls 40,000 invoice rows plus ~80,000 payment rows into the API process and reduces them per request. This is the hot path of the app's busiest page, on the same dyno that serves everything else; the bug being fixed (B12) was precisely that this set is bigger than a page.

This is a scale/latency risk rather than a wrong number — it is called out because the fix's own premise is "the open set is bigger than any cap", and it is the one place in the diff where that premise is answered by removing the cap rather than by aggregating.
findings.fixHint: Replace the findMany+reduce with a grouped SQL aggregate (SUM over the open set, bucketed by dueDate against the caller's `today`, netting CONFIRMED payments) alongside the avgDays query, or accept the read with an explicit ceiling + documented tenant-size bound.
findings.decision: The KPI read is an unbounded findMany with a nested payments select reduced in JS, on every /invoices load and every React Query invalidation, while the sibling avgDays leg proves a SQL aggregate was available. Not a wrong-output defect, but a real scaling regression versus the 999-row cap it replaced for the tenants B12 was meant to serve.

findings.summary: `awaitingConfirmationCount` counts DRAFT payments across every invoice status, including invoices the caller is not allowed to see — a CUSTOMER's tile can be non-zero while every invoice they can open has no draft payment.
findings.detail:
apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3010-3012: `this.prisma.forTenant().invoicePayment.count({ where: { status: "DRAFT", ...(customerId ? { invoice: { customerId } } : {}) } })`. There is no invoice-status restriction — unlike the sibling read three lines above, which narrows to `KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED`.

`findAll` explicitly hides DRAFT invoices from buyers (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:2823-2836: "Buyers must not see DRAFT invoices (not yet issued to them)"), and the KPI route is now open to `UserRole.CUSTOMER` (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.controller.ts:88-92), with the tile rendered unconditionally on the invoices page (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:577, no `isCustomer` guard, unlike :532/:814/:859).

Failure scenario: an operator records two unconfirmed (DRAFT) payments against a DRAFT invoice for buyer B. Buyer B opens `/invoices`: the list shows no DRAFT invoice at all (correctly), but the "Awaiting Confirmation" tile reads 2 with the hint "Draft payments not yet counted as paid" (page.tsx:296-315). The tile has no onClick, so the buyer has no row to reconcile it against — and its non-zero value discloses the existence of an invoice deliberately withheld from them. The same unscoped population applies to operators: the count spans payments on VOID and WRITTEN_OFF invoices, which every other tile in the bar excludes.
findings.fixHint: Narrow the count's `where` to the same open-invoice population the other tiles use (`invoice: { status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED }, ...(customerId ? { customerId } : {}) }`), so the tile counts only payments on invoices the caller can actually open.
findings.decision: awaitingConfirmationCount has no invoice-status restriction, so DRAFT payments on DRAFT invoices — which findAll deliberately hides from buyers — inflate a tile now served to CUSTOMER role and rendered unguarded; a buyer can see a non-zero count with no matching invoice. Real and a small information leak, distinct from the open CUSTOMER-403 blocker on the same route.

findings.summary: The REG-B110 e2e test — the only surviving web-side proof of B110 after T9 was withdrawn — asserts $0.00 against $0.00 and therefore passes identically on the buggy and the fixed build.
findings.detail:
The test provisions its own fixture: one customer, then one invoice via `POST /api/v1/invoices` (37-list-caps.spec.ts:307-315, `items: [{ description: "E2E B110 line", qty: 1, unitPrice: 250 }]`). `InvoicesService.create` hardcodes `status: InvoiceStatus.DRAFT` (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:507) and the DTO carries no status field, so the fixture invoice is always DRAFT and is never sent.

On the FIXED build, `getStatementForOperator` reads its open set as `where: { customerId, status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED } }` (customers.service.ts:~932) and `KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED` now includes `DRAFT` (invoice-status-sets.ts:36-41). So the DRAFT fixture is excluded and `statement.outstandingAmount === 0`. The spec then sets `const expected = fmtMoney(statement.outstandingAmount)` (line 331) = "$0.00" and asserts both the Profile-tab "Open Balance" tile and the Invoices-tab "Outstanding" card equal it.

On the PRE-FIX build the same two reads are also 0: the Profile tile already read `fmt(statement?.outstandingAmount ?? 0)` (customers/[id]/page.tsx:2390-2391) and the old Invoices-tab card reduced `allInvoices.filter(inv => ["SENT","VIEWED","PARTIAL","OVERDUE"].includes(inv.status))` — which also excludes DRAFT — over a single-invoice customer. Both render "$0.00", the assertion passes, and the test reports green against the defect it names.

The defect B110's web half is about is a page-scoped client reduce diverging from the whole-set server figure. Reproducing it needs (a) a non-DRAFT (sent) invoice so `outstandingAmount` is non-zero at all, and (b) more open invoices for that customer than one page of the Invoices tab, so the client reduce undercounts. The fixture has neither: one DRAFT invoice. With T9 explicitly withdrawn (build-plan.md P4, bug-test-plan.md T9), this is the only test anywhere covering the web leg of REG-B110, so reverting P4's `outstandingTotal = statement?.outstandingAmount ?? 0` change (customers/[id]/page.tsx:3540) back to the client-side reduce leaves the whole suite green.
findings.fixHint: Make the fixture non-vacuous: send the invoice (POST /invoices/:id/send, or create it via an order path that issues it) so outstandingAmount is non-zero, and create more open invoices for the fixture customer than one page of the Invoices tab renders, so the pre-fix client-side reduce genuinely disagrees with the statement figure. Then assert both tiles equal the API's own outstandingAmount.
findings.decision: The fixture is a single DRAFT invoice (create() hardcodes DRAFT, the DTO has no status), so the statement's open set excludes it and outstandingAmount is 0 on both builds; and even if DRAFT were counted, a one-invoice fixture cannot distinguish a capped read from an uncapped one, so the only surviving web-side REG-B110 proof cannot fail on the bug it claims to pin. A fixer must confirm which exclusion set the statement now uses, but the test is tautological under either.

findings.summary: The buyer wallet tile now reads the uncapped `availableCredit` while the credit rows beside it still come from the 50-row capped ledger, so the tile and its own "N active" sub-label can contradict each other — and `transactionsTruncated`, the flag added to disclose exactly this, is read on no buyer surface at all.
findings.detail:
This is the mobile half the earlier reader did not trace. `GET /buyer/statement` is served by `getStatementForOperator` (apps/api/src/buyer/buyer.controller.ts:248-255), the same method P3 changed, so the mobile customer app and the web buyer portal both inherit the new split.

After the change the two credit reads are no longer the same rows (customers.service.ts, getStatementForOperator):
- `openCreditNotes`: `where: { customerId, status: { not: "VOID" } }`, NO `take` — this feeds `availableCredit` (line ~1034).
- `ledgerCreditNotesRaw`: `where: { customerId }` (ALL statuses, VOID and expired included), `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }`, `take: LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP + 1` = 51, sliced to 50 — this feeds the `transactions` array.

Before the change both figures came from ONE read (`where: { customerId }, orderBy createdAt desc, take: 50`), so the tile and the rows always agreed (both under-reported together). They can now disagree.

Mobile consumer, apps/mobile/app/(customer)/payments.tsx:
- line 52 `const { data: statement } = useBuyerStatement();`
- line 66 `const credits = activeCreditRows(statement?.transactions);` — apps/mobile/lib/buyer-payments-logic.ts:34-36 filters `t.type === "CREDIT_NOTE" && t.runningBalance > 0.001` over the capped ledger rows.
- lines 112-116 render `Tile label="Store credit" value={money(statement?.availableCredit)} sub={credits.length > 0 ? `${credits.length} active` : "None available"}`.
- line 126 gates the whole "Active credits" card on `credits.length > 0`.

Failure scenario: a buyer has 3 open credit notes worth $50 each issued in January, and 55 credit notes issued since then that are fully used or VOID (`amount - amountUsed == 0`, so `runningBalance` is 0 on those rows). The uncapped `openCreditNotes` read still sums the 3 open ones → `availableCredit = 150`. The ledger read takes the 51 newest by `createdAt` — all of them used/VOID — and slices to 50, so no open note appears in `transactions`. `activeCreditRows` returns `[]`. The screen renders "Store credit $150.00 / None available" and omits the "Active credits" card entirely: the buyer is told they hold $150 of store credit and simultaneously that none is available, with no way to see which notes it is. Pre-change the tile would have read $0.00 — also wrong, but self-consistent, and B110's stated goal was the uncapped figure plus a labelled partial view.

The labelled-partial-view half never reaches this screen. `transactionsTruncated` IS emitted by the API and IS declared on the shared buyer type (packages/types/api/buyer.ts:104-105, non-optional `boolean`), and in the 55-used-note case above it is `true` (51 > 50). But a repo-wide grep for `transactionsTruncated` across apps/web and apps/mobile returns only: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/{ledger-truncation-note.tsx,page.tsx:3874}, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/customers/[id]/statement.tsx:138, plus the type declarations. Neither apps/mobile/app/(customer)/payments.tsx, nor apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/payments/page.tsx:145,253 (identical `activeCredits` filter + `fmt(statement?.availableCredit)` StatCard with the same "N active"/"None available" sub-label), nor apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/finances/page.tsx:106,181 reads it. Only the two OPERATOR statement surfaces disclose truncation; every BUYER-facing surface still presents the capped ledger as complete beside an uncapped total.

Separately answering the decider's third question: no mobile screen sums ledger rows into a money figure. `activeCreditRows` filters and never sums (buyer-payments-logic.ts header states this explicitly), the mobile operator statement screen renders `fmtMoney(Math.abs(t.runningBalance))` per row only, and the operator customer hub (apps/mobile/app/(operator)/customers/[id].tsx:222-249) reads server tiles verbatim. The contradiction is tile-vs-row-set, not tile-vs-recomputed-sum.
findings.fixHint: Decide the buyer disclosure: either render a truncation line on the buyer payments/finances surfaces (web + mobile) when `statement.transactionsTruncated` is true — the same shape as LedgerTruncationNote / the mobile operator statement line — or stop deriving the credit LIST from the capped all-status ledger and give the statement a dedicated uncapped open-credit-note array so the tile and its rows come from one source again.
findings.decision: GET /buyer/statement is served by the same getStatementForOperator P3 split, so the mobile wallet tile now reads the uncapped open-credit total while the rows and any 'N active' sub-label beside it come from a 50-row, all-status ledger — the two reads no longer share a basis and no mobile surface reads transactionsTruncated to label the partial view, which is the B110 design requirement. Fold into the already-open 'no consumer' fix rather than treating it as a separate defect.

findings.summary: The three sort-allowlist lookups this diff rewrites still use a bare index, so a prototype key (`sortBy=constructor`) resolves to an inherited value and reaches Prisma as a malformed orderBy (500) — while the sibling in this same diff, customers.service.ts, carries the Object.hasOwn guard that exists precisely for this.
findings.detail:
Pre-existing on master, but the batch rewrites these exact expressions for B169 and fixes the identical hazard one file over, so the sibling sweep stopped short.

The three rewritten sites:
- invoices.service.ts:2883-2888 (`findAll`): `const orderField = validSortFields[sortBy ?? ""] ?? "issueDate";` then `const orderBy: any = [{ [orderField]: orderDir }, { id: orderDir }];`
- invoices.service.ts:4464 (`listAllPayments`): `const orderBy = validSortFields[sortBy ?? ""] ?? [{ paidAt: "desc" }, { id: "desc" }];`
- invoices.service.ts:5595 (`exportPayments`): identical line.

`validSortFields` is a plain object literal, so its prototype chain is live. `??` only falls back on null/undefined, and an inherited value is neither. I confirmed the JS semantics with a Node probe this session:

  constructor -> function -> key: "function Object() { [native code] }"
  toString    -> function -> key: "function toString() { [native code] }"
  __proto__   -> object   -> key: "[object Object]"
  valueOf     -> function -> key: "function valueOf() { [native code] }"

Reachability: `ListInvoicesDto.sortBy` is a free `@IsOptional() @IsString() sortBy?: string` (apps/api/src/invoices/dto/list-invoices.dto.ts:29) with no `@IsIn`, and `listAllPayments`/`exportPayments` take `sortBy` straight off the query string as a raw `@Query("sortBy") sortBy?: string` (invoices.controller.ts:139-150). The route is open to OPERATOR and CUSTOMER (`@Get()` `@Roles(UserRole.OPERATOR, UserRole.CUSTOMER)`, controller class `@Roles(UserRole.OPERATOR)`).

Failure scenario: any authenticated operator or buyer issues `GET /api/v1/invoices?sortBy=constructor`. `validSortFields["constructor"]` resolves to `Object`, `??` does not fire, and Prisma receives `orderBy: [{ "function Object() { [native code] }": "desc" }, { id: "desc" }]` → PrismaClientValidationError. It is not an HttpException, so `SentryExceptionFilter` (extends `BaseExceptionFilter`, apps/api/src/common/sentry-exception.filter.ts:11) turns it into a 500 and reports it. `GET /api/v1/invoices/payments?sortBy=constructor` is worse: the whole `orderBy` becomes the `Object` function itself. `GET /api/v1/invoices/payments/export?sortBy=__proto__` hits the same line at 5595. Repeated calls are a cheap authenticated DoS plus Sentry flood.

The in-diff precedent and the exact fix shape are in the same commit: customers.service.ts:165-170 guards with `query.sortBy && Object.hasOwn(validSortFields, query.sortBy) ? validSortFields[query.sortBy] : undefined`, with the comment "Object.hasOwn (not a bare index) so prototype keys — __proto__, constructor, toString, valueOf… — can't resolve to a truthy inherited value and reach Prisma as a malformed orderBy (→ 500)", and its regression spec apps/api/src/customers/customers.security.spec.ts (F4-002) — which this diff also edits — enumerates exactly `["__proto__", "constructor", "toString", "valueOf", "hasOwnProperty"]`. No equivalent guard or spec exists for invoices.
findings.fixHint: Apply the customers.service.ts:165-170 shape to all three sites: gate the lookup on `Object.hasOwn(validSortFields, sortBy)` and fall back to the safe default otherwise, and add the F4-002-style `it.each(["__proto__","constructor","toString","valueOf","hasOwnProperty"])` coverage to invoices.service.spec.ts for findAll, listAllPayments and exportPayments.
findings.decision: validSortFields is a plain object literal, so sortBy=constructor resolves to Object.prototype.constructor (neither null nor undefined), survives the ?? fallback and reaches Prisma as a malformed orderBy key — a reproducible 500 on all three rewritten sites, while the customers.service.ts sibling in this same diff got the Object.hasOwn guard. Pre-existing, no money or data exposure, but the sweep stopped one file short.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` is computed from the OPEN-set read lengths but the ledger it describes is read over ALL rows, so it reports `false` for a ledger that is in fact truncated.
confirmedFindings.detail: In `getStatementForOperator`, `ledgerInvoices` queries `where: { customerId }` with `take: LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP (100)` — no status filter — while `openInvoices` queries `status: { notIn: CREDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE }` uncapped. The flag at :1021-1024 compares `openInvoices.length > 100`. Failure: a customer with 400 invoices of which 380 are PAID/VOID/WRITTEN_OFF and 20 open → `ledgerInvoices` returns the 100 most-recent of 400 (300 rows dropped) but `openInvoices.length` is 20, so the response says `transactionsTruncated: false` while `transactions` is a partial view. Same for credit notes (`openCreditNotes` excludes only VOID vs a ledger over all credit notes, cap 50) and advances (`openAdvancePayments` is `balance > 0` vs a ledger over all advances, cap 50). Identical defect in `getMyStatement` at :359-360 (caps 50/50). The flag can only ever be a false negative, and the miss is the common case (most customers accumulate settled invoices). This is exactly the case the cause-ruling §2 and bug-test-plan T4 define the flag for — "true when the capped list is shorter than the count" — and the T4 spec does not catch it because its `honouringTake` mock returns the same 150 all-SENT rows for both the open and ledger reads, so open == all in the fixture.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Derive the flag from the LEDGER reads' own populations, not the open sets: add `invoice.count({ where: { customerId } })` / `creditNote.count({ where: { customerId } })` / `advancePayment.count({ where: { customerId } })` to the existing `Promise.all` and compare each against its cap (or, cheaper, `ledgerX.length === CAP`, accepting an off-by-one over-report when the count equals the cap exactly). Extend the T4 spec so the ledger fixture is strictly larger than the open fixture (e.g. 300 PAID + 20 SENT), which is what makes the two bases distinguishable.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new literal-UTC day-end bounds string-concatenate the raw query param, so a full ISO-8601 datetime — which the DTOs accept — now produces an Invalid Date instead of a usable bound.
confirmedFindings.detail: `where.issueDate.lte = new Date(`${dateTo}T23:59:59.999Z`)` (:2820) and `where.dueDate.lte = new Date(`${dueTo}T23:59:59.999Z`)` (:2831) assume `dateTo`/`dueTo` are exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`, but `ListInvoicesDto` declares `dateFrom`/`dateTo` as `@IsString()` (no format check) and `dueFrom`/`dueTo` as `@IsDateString()`, which accepts a full ISO datetime. `GET /api/v1/invoices?dueTo=2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z` passes validation and yields `new Date("2026-08-26T00:00:00.000ZT23:59:59.999Z")` — I confirmed in node this session that this is `Invalid Date` — which is then handed to Prisma as a `lte` bound; before this change the same request produced a valid (host-local, buggy, but working) instant and returned rows. The `paidAt` legs have the same shape: `tenantCalendarDayStart(dateFrom, tz)` (:4357, :5489) does `new Date(`${dateStr}T00:00:00.000Z`)` on `dateFrom` read straight off `@Query("dateFrom")` with no DTO at all on `GET /invoices/payments` and `@Query() query: any` on `/invoices/payments/export`. I checked every shipped caller (web invoices page URL filters and finance/payments page `<input type="date">`; no mobile invoice/payment date filters) and all send date-only strings, so no current UI hits this — it is a robustness/contract regression on an input the DTOs advertise as valid, not a live break.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Normalize the incoming value to a calendar date before composing the instant (e.g. `const day = dateTo.slice(0, 10)` after a `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/` check, or reuse `calendarDateFromIso(new Date(dateTo))`), and reject a value that isn't a parsable date rather than letting an Invalid Date reach Prisma. Tightening the DTOs (`@Matches(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/)` like the new `KpiSummaryDto`) is the alternative, but it is a narrowing of an accepted input and needs the same decision.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` is derived from the OPEN-set size instead of the ledger query's own row count, so it reports `false` for the most common truncated-ledger case — and T4's fixture cannot tell the two bases apart, so the test claims coverage it does not have.
confirmedFindings.detail: The ledger reads are `invoice.findMany({ where: { customerId } , take: 100 })` / `creditNote.findMany({ where: { customerId }, take: 50 })` / `advancePayment.findMany({ where: { customerId }, take: 50 })` — no status filter, i.e. the WHOLE history. But the flag is computed as `openInvoices.length > LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP || openCreditNotes.length > LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP || openAdvancePayments.length > LEDGER_ADVANCE_CAP`, where `openInvoices` excludes PAID/VOID/WRITTEN_OFF, `openCreditNotes` excludes VOID and `openAdvancePayments` requires `balance > 0`. Failure scenario: a long-lived customer with 400 invoices of which 390 are PAID and 10 open → `ledgerInvoices` is truncated 400→100, but `openInvoices.length` is 10, so `transactionsTruncated` is `false` and the response asserts a complete ledger that is 75% missing. Same for a customer with 200 fully-consumed advances (balance 0) and 5 live ones. cause-ruling.md §2 specifies `transactionsTruncated` as "true when the capped list is shorter than the count" — the count of the list that was capped, not of the open subset. The identical bug is at `getMyStatement` (customers.service.ts:359-360, caps 50/50). It cannot be caught by T4 (customers.service.spec.ts:1191): its fixture makes all 150 invoices / 60 credit notes / 60 advances open, so open-count and ledger-count are the same number and the assertion `transactionsTruncated: true` passes under either basis — the test-plan row claims to prove the flag but does not exercise the distinguishing case.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Base the flag on the capped read itself — e.g. `ledgerInvoices.length === LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP` (a full page means there may be more), or add `invoice.count({ where: { customerId } })` and compare — and make the same change in `getMyStatement`. Then extend the T4 fixture with settled rows (e.g. 150 PAID + 5 open invoices) so the open-count basis fails.

confirmedFindings.summary: `InvoiceKpiSummary` is never re-exported from the `@routeflow/types` barrel and the API re-declares its shape inline, so build-plan P1's "shared response type" is not actually shared or pinned between the two sides.
confirmedFindings.detail: `packages/types/index.ts` re-exports every other `api/*.ts` module (`./api/enums`, `./api/orders`, `./api/customers`, `./api/products`, `./api/finance`, `./api/returns`, `./api/regulated`, `./api/routes`, `./api/buyer`, `./api/misc` at lines 144-153) but has no `export * from "./api/invoices"`. As a result `apps/web/lib/api/invoices.ts:21` imports it by the deep path `@routeflow/types/api/invoices` — a pattern with no other occurrence anywhere in the repo (grep returns exactly that one line) and contrary to CLAUDE.md's "imported via `@routeflow/types` — never redeclare one a second time". Worse, `InvoicesService.getKpiSummary` (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:2916-2923) declares its return type as an inline six-field object literal rather than importing the shared interface, precisely to avoid the missing barrel line. Failure scenario: a future field added or renamed on the server's inline return type compiles cleanly while `InvoiceKpiSummary` and the web hook keep the old shape — the exact untyped-mirror drift class CLAUDE.md/L-072 warn about — and nothing fails `check-types` on either side. (Verified not a build risk today: the web import is `import type`, erased before webpack, and `transpilePackages` already lists `@routeflow/types`; `apps/web` tsc and jest are green.)
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `export * from "./api/invoices";` to packages/types/index.ts, change apps/web/lib/api/invoices.ts:21 to import from `@routeflow/types`, and have `getKpiSummary` return `Promise<InvoiceKpiSummary>` so the two sides are pinned to one declaration.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` was never registered in the shared types, which the test plan's Harness notes explicitly required — no client type exposes the field, so no UI can label the partial view without a cast.
confirmedFindings.detail: bug-test-plan.md's Harness notes (line 27) require: "Register `useInvoiceKpiSummary`, `search` on `useOrders`, and `transactionsTruncated` in the shared types." The first two were delivered (apps/web/lib/api/invoices.ts:247, apps/web/lib/api/orders.ts:186). The third was not: `BuyerStatement` in packages/types/api/buyer.ts:96-106 still declares only `outstandingAmount / overdueAmount / availableCredit / advanceBalance / pendingOrdersAmount / transactions`, and the web-local `CustomerStatement` in apps/web/lib/api/customers.ts:222 likewise lacks it. A grep for `transactionsTruncated` across the whole worktree returns only the two API service sites, the API spec, and the planning docs — zero web or mobile consumers. Failure scenario: the API now returns a truncation flag that every typed client silently discards, so cause-ruling.md §2's "or it is labelled a partial view" half of the invariant is unreachable for the customer statement; a developer wiring the label has to cast through `any` (as the spec itself does at customers.service.spec.ts:1255).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `transactionsTruncated: boolean;` to `BuyerStatement` (packages/types/api/buyer.ts) and to `CustomerStatement` (apps/web/lib/api/customers.ts:222), or fold the web-local interface into the shared one.

confirmedFindings.summary: T1-pin's stated `exportPayments` paidAt-bounds assertion was not delivered, leaving the second of the two `paidAt` sites B89 changed with no behavioral test.
confirmedFindings.detail: bug-test-plan.md T1-pin says the pin covers "`exportPayments` uses the same paidAt bounds". `exportPayments` (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:5480-5492) did receive the same change — `tenantCalendarDayStart(dateFrom, tz)` / `endOfCalendarDay(dateTo, tz)` replacing the host-local `setHours(23,59,59,999)` — but no spec asserts it. Grepping `exportPayments` in invoices.service.spec.ts returns exactly three hits (lines 5658, 5684, 5707): a CSV Bank-Date-column test, its `.split` read, and the `settledAt` orderBy pin. The new REG-B89 describe (line 3251) only exercises `listAllPayments` and `findAll`. Failure scenario: re-introducing `const end = new Date(dateTo); end.setHours(23,59,59,999)` in `exportPayments` alone leaves the entire api suite green (I ran it: 884/884 pass), so the CSV export's tenant-local day window is unprotected against exactly the regression this batch fixed, on a host whose local TZ is UTC (CI included).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a third `it` to the REG-B89 describe that calls `service.exportPayments({ dateFrom: "2026-08-26", dateTo: "2026-08-26" })` under the same America/New_York `resolveTenantInvoiceDefaults` mock and asserts `where.paidAt` equals `{ gte: new Date("2026-08-26T04:00:00.000Z"), lte: new Date("2026-08-27T03:59:59.999Z") }`.

confirmedFindings.summary: B110's `getMyStatement` half — an explicit build-plan P3 requirement ("same for `getMyStatement`") — has no regression test; reverting just that half leaves the suite green.
confirmedFindings.detail: build-plan.md P3 and cause-ruling.md §2 both require the uncapped OPEN-set money reads "In `getStatementForOperator` (and `getMyStatement`)", and `getMyStatement` was in fact rewritten (customers.service.ts:276-360: new uncapped `openInvoices`/`openCreditNotes` reads, `sumConfirmed` basis, `transactionsTruncated`). But the T4 describe (line 1191) is titled and scoped to `getStatementForOperator` only, and the two pre-existing `getMyStatement` tests (lines 991 and 1031) use `prisma.invoice.findMany.mockResolvedValue([...])` with one to three rows — a mock that ignores `take` entirely, which the plan's own Harness note calls out as making such a test vacuous. Failure scenario: restore the `take: 50` cap on `getMyStatement`'s invoice/credit-note reads and point the money reduces back at them; `npx jest src/customers` still passes, and the buyer-facing outstanding/availableCredit figures silently under-report again for any buyer with more than 50 open invoices. The probe plan (cause-ruling.md §7) maps `customers.service.ts` → REG-B110 (T4), so the probe would not catch this either.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Mirror the T4 fixture for `getMyStatement`: a `honouringTake` invoice/creditNote mock with 150/60 open rows through `service.getMyStatement(customerPayload)`, asserting `outstandingAmount === 1500` and `availableCredit === 300`.

confirmedFindings.summary: T6 (REG-B12) never exercises getKpiSummary's payment basis — every mocked invoice row has `payments: []`, so the `sumConfirmed` balance math is a surviving mutant.
confirmedFindings.detail: All four rows in the `REG-B12 — getKpiSummary()` behavioral `it` are `{ total, dueDate, payments: [] }`. `getKpiSummary` computes `const balance = Math.max(0, Number(inv.total) - sumConfirmed(inv.payments))` (invoices.service.ts, new method). With empty payment arrays `sumConfirmed` is always 0, so replacing that line with `const balance = Number(inv.total)` — or with the historical buggy `p.status !== "VOID"` basis that F03 fixed at ~15 sites — still yields totalOutstanding 185 / overdue 100 / dueToday 50 / dueIn30 25 and the suite stays green. Concretely: a PARTIAL invoice with total 100 and payments `[{amount:40,status:"DRAFT"},{amount:20,status:"PAID"}]` must contribute 80 to Total Outstanding; nothing in this change (unit, RTL, or e2e — T8(a) only compares the rendered tile to the same endpoint's own number, so both would be wrong together) asserts that. This is the one money figure B12 exists to make correct.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a row with mixed DRAFT/VOID/PAID payments to the T6 fixture (e.g. total 100, payments [40 DRAFT, 30 VOID, 20 PAID]) and raise the expected totalOutstanding/bucket figures by 80, mirroring the CONFIRMED-basis oracle already used in customers.service.spec.ts's T4 second `it`.

confirmedFindings.summary: `getMyStatement` got the same B110 behavior change (CONFIRMED payment basis, uncapped open reads, transactionsTruncated) with zero REG coverage — its two existing tests pass under both the old and new basis.
confirmedFindings.detail: The diff changes `getMyStatement` exactly like `getStatementForOperator`: `amountPaid` moves from `payments.filter(p => p.status !== "VOID")` to `sumConfirmed(...)` (PAID-only), the invoice/credit-note reads split into uncapped open-set + capped ledger, and `transactionsTruncated` is added. T4 pins all of that only for `getStatementForOperator`. The two existing `getMyStatement` tests (customers.service.spec.ts:991 availableCredit, :1031 "a VOID payment does not reduce outstanding/overdue") use only PAID and VOID payment rows, so both are green under the old `!== "VOID"` basis too. Failure scenario: revert `withPaid` in `getMyStatement` alone to the old filter and the entire suite still passes, while a buyer viewing their own portal statement sees outstandingAmount under-reported by the full amount of any unconfirmed DRAFT payment (invoice total 100, DRAFT payment 40 → 60 shown instead of 100). The same revert is caught for the operator twin, so the coverage is asymmetric on identical money code.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a `getMyStatement` sibling of T4's DRAFT/VOID/PAID `it` (invoice total 100, payments [40 DRAFT, 30 VOID, 20 PAID] → outstandingAmount 80) plus a take-honouring findMany fixture proving the >50-invoice open set is summed whole.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` is asserted only on the `true` side, and the predicate it pins counts the OPEN set while the ledger read is unfiltered — so a truncated ledger reports `false` and no test notices.
confirmedFindings.detail: T4 asserts `transactionsTruncated: true` in a single scenario and nowhere asserts `false`, so a hardcoded `return true` passes. Worse, the predicate the test blesses is wrong for what the flag claims: in `getStatementForOperator` it is `openInvoices.length > 100 || openCreditNotes.length > 50 || openAdvancePayments.length > 50` (customers.service.ts:1021), but the ledger rows actually rendered come from `invoice.findMany({ where: { customerId }, take: 100 })` — ALL statuses, no open filter. Failure scenario: a customer with 60 open (SENT) invoices and 200 PAID invoices — the ledger shows 100 of 260 transactions (silently truncated, exactly the B110 class) while `transactionsTruncated` is `false` because 60 <= 100. Same shape at customers.service.ts:359 for `getMyStatement` (caps 50/50) and for the advance-payment leg (`balance: { gt: 0 }` open set vs an unfiltered `take: 50` ledger). Note also that grep finds no web or mobile consumer of `transactionsTruncated` at all, so nothing outside this one assertion exercises it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide whether the flag describes the ledger or the open set, then add the missing negative case (small customer → `false`) and a mixed case (few open, many settled) that distinguishes the two predicates; if it should describe the ledger, compare each ledger array's length to its own cap.

confirmedFindings.summary: T6's avgDays oracle is tautological — the mock returns 12.5 and the test asserts 12.5; the aging SQL and its `?? 0` null path have no coverage anywhere.
confirmedFindings.detail: `prisma.$queryRaw.mockResolvedValue([{ avgDays: 12.5 }])` followed by `expect(result).toEqual({ ..., avgDays: 12.5, ... })` only proves the value is passed through. The only non-vacuous assertion about the raw query is `expect(prisma.$queryRaw.mock.calls[0]).toContain("test-tenant")` (tenant id bound, not interpolated) — nothing pins `status = 'PAID'`, the `paidAt IS NOT NULL` / `sentAt IS NOT NULL` guards, or the /86400 day conversion, so the query could silently average the wrong population. The `avgDays: avgDaysRows[0]?.avgDays ?? 0` branch is also untested: a tenant with no PAID invoices makes Postgres `AVG` return NULL, and that `?? 0` is what makes the web tile render "N/A" (invoices/page.tsx:295 `kpis.avgDays > 0 ? ... : "N/A"`). A mutation to `?? null` passes today and would render "N/A" only by accident of `null > 0`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add an `it` with `$queryRaw` resolving `[{ avgDays: null }]` (and one with `[]`) asserting `avgDays === 0`, and assert the query text contains the PAID/paidAt/sentAt predicates.

confirmedFindings.summary: T6 has no edge rows: no null dueDate, no status-OVERDUE-with-future-dueDate, and no day-30/day-31 boundary — so an unasserted behavior change from the client memo it replaces ships untested.
confirmedFindings.detail: The four fixture rows are all unpaid with concrete dueDates 1 day before / on / 15 days after `today`. Three real edges are uncovered: (1) `dueDate: null` — `getKpiSummary` does `if (dueDateIso == null) continue;`, so such an invoice counts toward totalOutstanding but no bucket; nothing asserts that. (2) The client memo this replaces bucketed by `inv.status === "OVERDUE" || (due && due < today && open)`; the new server code buckets purely by date, so an invoice with `status: "OVERDUE"` and a dueDate 10 days out now lands in dueIn30 instead of overdue — a real change in what the Overdue tile shows, with no test either way. (3) `dueIn30` uses `dueDateIso <= cutoff` where cutoff = today+30; no row sits on day 30 or day 31, so an off-by-one in `addCalendarDays` would survive.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add rows for dueDate null, status OVERDUE with a future dueDate, and dueDate exactly today+30 and today+31, with the intended bucket for each stated in the oracle.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` is computed from the OPEN-set counts but describes the ALL-STATUS capped ledger, so it reports `false` while the ledger is silently truncated.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Both statement methods build the ledger from a different population than the flag that labels it.

`getMyStatement` (:301-320, :359-360): `ledgerInvoices` reads `where: { customerId }` with NO status filter and `take: LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP` (50); `openInvoices` reads `status: { notIn: CREDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE }` uncapped. The flag is `openInvoices.length > 50 || openCreditNotes.length > 50`. A customer with 30 OPEN invoices and 200 PAID ones: the ledger returns 50 of 230 rows (180 hidden) but `30 > 50` is false, so the response says `transactionsTruncated: false` on a ledger that IS truncated. Since almost every invoice eventually becomes PAID, this false negative is the normal case for any established customer, not an edge case.

`getStatementForOperator` (:934-970, :1021-1024) has the same defect three times over: `ledgerInvoices` = all statuses take 100 vs `openInvoices` = open only; `ledgerCreditNotes` = all statuses take 50 vs `openCreditNotes` = `status: { not: "VOID" }`; `ledgerAdvancePayments` = all rows take 50 vs `openAdvancePayments` = `balance: { gt: 0 }`. A customer with 200 fully-consumed advance payments and 3 with balance > 0 gets a 50-row truncated advance ledger and `transactionsTruncated: false`.

This breaks the ruling's stated invariant (cause-ruling.md §2: a figure "is computed by the database over the WHOLE set, or it is labelled a partial view") — the new label is wrong in the direction that hides the truncation. Nothing in web/mobile consumes the field yet (grep for `transactionsTruncated` across apps/web + apps/mobile returns nothing), so no user sees it today, but it ships as an API contract that a later UI will wire against a broken oracle. Verified: `npx jest src/customers` is green, i.e. no existing test pins this value.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Derive the flag from the population the ledger actually reads: either compare `ledgerInvoices.length === LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP` (etc.) or add `invoice.count({ where: { customerId } })` / `creditNote.count` / `advancePayment.count` alongside the capped reads and compare against those. Apply the same correction at both :359-360 and :1021-1024.

confirmedFindings.summary: `getKpiSummary`'s SQL average drops the client memo's `days >= 0` guard, so a PAID invoice re-sent after payment feeds a large negative into "Avg. Days to Get Paid".
confirmedFindings.detail:
The deleted client memo (invoices/page.tsx, removed at :318-325 of the old file) computed `days = round(paidAt - sentAt)` and counted it only `if (days >= 0)`. The replacement at :2935-2942 is `AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ("paidAt" - "sentAt")) / 86400)` over every PAID invoice with both stamps — no sign guard.

A negative delta is reachable through a normal operation: `send()` (:3458-3475) explicitly supports re-sending an already-settled invoice ("Idempotent on re-send… Re-sending an invoice that credit auto-apply already made PAID/PARTIAL must NOT downgrade it") and unconditionally writes `sentAt: new Date()` while leaving `paidAt` alone. An operator who re-sends a paid invoice as a receipt copy 90 days after payment leaves a row with `paidAt - sentAt = -90 days`.

Concrete failure: a tenant with 10 PAID invoices averaging 12 days plus one re-sent-after-payment invoice at -90 now renders (10*12 - 90)/11 ≈ 3 days instead of 12; with a handful of such rows the mean goes ≤ 0 and page.tsx:295 (`kpis.avgDays > 0 ? ... : "N/A"`) renders "N/A" — the tile B12 was meant to fix now reads blank on a tenant that has the data.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add the sign guard to the SQL predicate — e.g. `AND "paidAt" >= "sentAt"` alongside the existing `paidAt IS NOT NULL AND sentAt IS NOT NULL` — so the server reproduces the memo's own basis.

confirmedFindings.summary: A `today` value that matches the DTO regex but is not a real calendar date throws a RangeError inside `getKpiSummary`, returning 500 after three DB queries have already run.
confirmedFindings.detail:
`KpiSummaryDto` validates `today` with `@Matches(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/)` only (apps/api/src/invoices/dto/kpi-summary.dto.ts:9). The global pipe (main.ts:145-149, `whitelist`/`transform`/`forbidNonWhitelisted`) runs it, so the regex is the whole gate.

`GET /api/v1/invoices/kpi-summary?today=2026-13-01` passes that regex. At :2948, `addCalendarDays(new Date("2026-13-01T00:00:00.000Z"), 30).toISOString()` throws — I confirmed this in node: `2026-13-01`, `9999-99-99` and `0000-00-00` all throw `RangeError: Invalid time value`. Because the throw is AFTER the `await Promise.all([...])` at :2923, the unbounded open-set `findMany`, the `invoicePayment.count` and the `$queryRaw` all execute first, then the request 500s.

A near miss is worse than a crash: `today=2026-02-30` does not throw (verified: it silently rolls to `2026-03-02`, cutoff `2026-04-01`), so the tiles bucket against a calendar day the caller never asked for while returning 200.

Operator-only endpoint (class `@Roles(UserRole.OPERATOR)`, no method override — authorization itself is correct), so this is an unhandled-input 500, not a data-exposure path.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Reject a non-existent calendar date in the DTO or at the top of `getKpiSummary` (parse and check `Number.isNaN(t.getTime())` plus round-trip `toISOString().slice(0,10) === today`) and throw `BadRequestException` before any query runs.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new `$queryRaw` binds a possibly-null tenantId while its two sibling reads in the same `Promise.all` go unscoped, so one response can mix all-tenant totals with a zeroed average.
confirmedFindings.detail:
`getKpiSummary` takes `const tenantId = this.prisma.getTenantId()` at :2921 and binds it into the raw SQL at :2939 without a null guard. Every other `getTenantId()` call in this file guards it — :121-122 (`if (!tenantId || ...) return`), :205-206 (`if (!tenantId) return { ... }`).

`PrismaService.getTenantId()` is documented to return null exactly for SUPER_ADMIN / unset context (prisma/prisma.service.ts:35-38), and `forTenant()` on a null tenantId returns the UNSCOPED client (prisma.service.ts:296-299, "SUPER_ADMIN (tenantId === null): returns unscoped `this` — full DB access").

So for a caller with no tenant context, the two Prisma reads (`invoice.findMany`, `invoicePayment.count`) aggregate across every tenant, while the raw query's `"tenantId" = NULL` matches nothing and yields `avgDays: 0`. One response then reports a cross-tenant `totalOutstanding`/`overdue`/`dueToday` next to a hard 0 average — an internally inconsistent figure rather than an obvious error. The all-tenant behaviour of the two Prisma reads matches the pre-existing convention for SUPER_ADMIN; the new inconsistency is that the third read does not follow it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the intended SUPER_ADMIN semantics and make all three reads agree — either guard `if (!tenantId) return <zeroed summary>` at the top (matching :205-206's pattern), or make the raw query fall back to no tenant predicate when tenantId is null.

confirmedFindings.summary: Date-window bounds are built by string-concatenating unvalidated query params, so an ISO-8601 datetime that these endpoints previously accepted now yields an Invalid Date.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Three sites now append a time suffix to a raw request string instead of parsing it:
- :2820 `where.issueDate.lte = new Date(`${dateTo}T23:59:59.999Z`)` — `ListInvoicesDto.dateTo` is only `@IsString()` (dto/list-invoices.dto.ts:26), so any string passes.
- :2831 `where.dueDate.lte = new Date(`${dueTo}T23:59:59.999Z`)` — `dueTo` is `@IsDateString()` (dto/list-invoices.dto.ts:29), a validator that explicitly accepts full ISO-8601 datetimes.
- :228-231 `tenantCalendarDayStart(dateStr, tz)` does `new Date(`${dateStr}T00:00:00.000Z`)`, reached from :4357 and :5489 with `dateFrom` read straight off the query string with NO DTO at all (invoices.controller.ts:141-142 uses bare `@Query("dateFrom")`).

Verified in node: `new Date("2026-09-07T00:00:00.000Z" + "T23:59:59.999Z")` is `Invalid Date`. So `GET /invoices/payments?dateFrom=2026-09-07T00:00:00Z` now hands an Invalid Date to Prisma's `paidAt.gte`, where the previous `new Date(dateFrom)` produced a working filter. I confirmed the Invalid Date; I did not execute Prisma against it, so I can only say the previously-working filter is gone, not the exact error surface.

The breakage is also asymmetric in a way that will confuse whoever hits it: on the paidAt path a full-ISO `dateTo` still works (`endOfCalendarDay` parses it) and only `dateFrom` breaks; on `issueDate` it is the reverse. Every in-repo caller I checked sends `YYYY-MM-DD` (web date inputs; mobile `invoices/[id].tsx:130` uses `issueDate.slice(0,10)`), so this is reachable through the documented Swagger/API surface rather than the shipped UI.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Parse the incoming value rather than concatenating — normalise to a calendar date first (e.g. `calendarDateFromIso(raw)` from common/calendar-date.ts, rejecting `""`) and build the bound from that, and give `listAllPayments`/`exportPayments` a DTO that pins `dateFrom`/`dateTo` to `YYYY-MM-DD` the way `KpiSummaryDto.today` does.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new GET /invoices/kpi-summary route is OPERATOR-only, but the KPI bar it now feeds is rendered unconditionally on a page CUSTOMER-role users are explicitly allowed to open, so buyers get a 403 and six money tiles silently render $0.00.
confirmedFindings.detail: `@Get("kpi-summary")` declares no method-level `@Roles`, so it inherits the controller's class-level `@Roles(UserRole.OPERATOR)` (invoices.controller.ts:43-44). `RolesGuard` (apps/api/src/auth/guards/roles.guard.ts) maps `ROLE_SATISFIES[CUSTOMER] = [CUSTOMER]`, so a CUSTOMER token can never satisfy OPERATOR → 403. Meanwhile apps/web/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:236 puts `/invoices` in `CUSTOMER_ALLOWED` and CUSTOMER_NAV (layout.tsx:165) links to it, and apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:577 renders `<PaymentSummaryBar />` with no `!isCustomer` guard (the page's other customer branches are at 532/814/859). The endpoint this replaced — `useInvoices({ limit: 999 })` → `@Get()` with `@Roles(OPERATOR, CUSTOMER)` — was allowed for buyers and scoped to their own invoices (invoices.service.ts:2789-2800). Scenario: a CUSTOMER user with $4,200 of open invoices opens /invoices; `useInvoiceKpiSummary` 403s, `apiClient`'s interceptor only special-cases 401/PLAN_GATE so the error is swallowed, and `const kpis = summary ?? {zeros}` (page.tsx:243) renders Total Outstanding $0.00, Overdue $0.00, Due Today $0.00 to a buyer who owes money — with no error state anywhere. Nothing in the api or web test suites covers the CUSTOMER role on this bar.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the contract: either gate the bar (`{!isCustomer && <PaymentSummaryBar .../>}`), or open the route to CUSTOMER — but note that simply adding `UserRole.CUSTOMER` to `@Roles` would leak the WHOLE tenant's receivables to a buyer, because `getKpiSummary(today)` takes no `JwtPayload` and applies no `customerId` scope; that path needs `@CurrentUser()` plus the same customer lookup + DRAFT exclusion `findAll` does at invoices.service.ts:2789-2803.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` is computed from the OPEN-set counts while the ledger it describes is a cap over ALL rows, so it reports "not truncated" for exactly the common case where the ledger really is truncated.
confirmedFindings.detail: `ledgerInvoices` is `findMany({ where: { customerId }, take: LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP })` — no status filter, all invoices (line ~907). The flag is `openInvoices.length > LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP || openCreditNotes.length > LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP || openAdvancePayments.length > LEDGER_ADVANCE_CAP` (line 1021), i.e. it measures the *open* sets against caps that were applied to the *all-status* reads. Scenario: a long-standing customer with 500 invoices of which 480 are PAID and 20 open — `getStatementForOperator` returns a ledger holding 100 of 500 rows (truncated in fact) with `transactionsTruncated: false`; same shape in `getMyStatement` at line 359 (50 of N). Because most invoices eventually reach PAID, the false-negative is the normal case, not the edge case. The T4 spec at customers.service.spec.ts:1203-1260 makes every fixture `status: "SENT"`, so open count == total count and the mis-computation is invisible to it.

confirmedFindings.summary: The avgDays raw query averages `paidAt - sentAt` with no non-negative guard, so a re-sent paid invoice contributes a large negative duration and can drive the "Avg. Days to Get Paid" tile to N/A.
confirmedFindings.detail: `SELECT AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ("paidAt" - "sentAt")) / 86400)` filters only on `status = 'PAID' AND paidAt IS NOT NULL AND sentAt IS NOT NULL`. `sentAt` is re-stamped unconditionally on every send — `data: { status: nextStatus, sentAt: new Date() }` at invoices.service.ts:3474 (`send`) and :3680 (`sendEmail`), where `nextStatus` deliberately stays PAID for a non-DRAFT invoice — so re-sending an already-paid invoice as a receipt makes `sentAt > paidAt`. The client memo this replaced explicitly discarded those rows (`if (days >= 0)` in the deleted block of apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx). Scenario: a tenant with 10 paid invoices averaging 12 days; an operator re-sends 3 paid invoices from six months ago, each now contributing about −180 days; the average goes negative and page.tsx:295 (`kpis.avgDays > 0 ? ... : "N/A"`) renders "N/A" for a tenant that has plenty of paid history. The T6 spec mocks `$queryRaw` and asserts only the pass-through value, so no test constrains the SQL's own semantics.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the intended basis and encode it in SQL — most directly `AND "paidAt" >= "sentAt"` in the WHERE (matching the old `days >= 0` filter); if instead the first-send instant is what's wanted, that requires a column that is not re-stamped, which is a bigger call.

confirmedFindings.summary: Day-window bounds are now built by string concatenation onto the raw query param, so a date value carrying a time component — which the DTOs accept — produces an Invalid Date instead of the working instant it produced before.
confirmedFindings.detail: `new Date(`${dateTo}T23:59:59.999Z`)` (line 2820), the identical `dueTo` line (2831), and `tenantCalendarDayStart`'s `new Date(`${dateStr}T00:00:00.000Z`)` (line 229, used for `paidAt.gte` at 4357 and 5489) all assume a bare `YYYY-MM-DD`. Verified in node on this tree: `new Date("2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z" + "T23:59:59.999Z")` → Invalid Date, where the replaced `new Date(dateTo); setHours(23,59,59,999)` returned `2026-08-26T04:59:59.999Z`. `ListInvoicesDto.dateTo` is `@IsString()` and `dueTo` is `@IsDateString()` (which accepts full ISO 8601 datetimes), and `@Get("payments")` / `@Get("payments/export")` read `dateFrom`/`dateTo` straight off the query string with no DTO at all (invoices.controller.ts:90, 135-145). Scenario: `GET /invoices?dueTo=2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z` (a URL a user can bookmark or an API client can build from an ISO timestamp) previously returned the due-window page; it now reaches Prisma as `dueDate: { lte: Invalid Date }`. No current in-repo caller sends this shape (web chips and the mobile sibling lookup both slice to 10 chars), so this is a latent robustness regression rather than a live break.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Normalize once at the boundary — slice/validate to `YYYY-MM-DD` (or reuse `calendarDateFromIso`) before composing the instant — and tighten `dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`dueFrom`/`dueTo` to a `@Matches(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/)` shape like the new `KpiSummaryDto.today` already uses.

confirmedFindings.summary: `transactionsTruncated` is derived from the OPEN-set counts while the ledger queries it describes are capped over the customer's FULL invoice/credit-note/advance set, so it reports `false` for a ledger that is in fact truncated.
confirmedFindings.detail: At `:359` (getMyStatement) and `:1021` (getStatementForOperator) the flag is `openInvoices.length > LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP || openCreditNotes.length > LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP (|| openAdvancePayments.length > LEDGER_ADVANCE_CAP)`. But `ledgerInvoices` is `findMany({ where: { customerId }, take: LEDGER_INVOICE_CAP })` — no status filter — and `ledgerCreditNotes` / `ledgerAdvancePayments` likewise read the unfiltered set. Failure scenario: a long-standing customer with 500 invoices of which 480 are PAID and 20 open. `openInvoices.length` is 20, so `transactionsTruncated` is `false`, while the ledger shows only the 100 most recent of 500 rows. The same asymmetry applies to credit notes (`status: { not: "VOID" }` open read vs unfiltered ledger read) and advance payments (`balance: { gt: 0 }` vs unfiltered). The flag can also fire spuriously in the mirror case (open credit notes > 50 while the ledger cap is met exactly).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Derive truncation from the ledger reads themselves — e.g. `take: CAP + 1` on each ledger query and set the flag when a read comes back longer than its cap (then slice) — rather than from the open-set counts.

confirmedFindings.summary: Two different definitions of the open receivables set now coexist: the new `KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED` (excludes DRAFT) for the invoices KPI, and `CREDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE` (keeps DRAFT) for both statements — and P4 just repointed the customer Invoices-tab Outstanding card onto the DRAFT-including one.

confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide one open-receivables definition for aggregate money figures and use it in both places — either switch the statements' figure reads to `KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED` (dropping DRAFT, matching the invoices KPI and the card's previous behavior) or document why the per-customer figure deliberately counts DRAFT and leave the card on its old filter.
