remainingFindings.summary: `availableCredit` is now computed from an uncapped credit-note read while three buyer-portal surfaces still derive the buyer's *list and count* of usable credits from the still-capped 50-row `transactions` ledger, so the wallet tile and the credits beside it can now contradict each other.
remainingFindings.detail:
`getStatementForOperator` is what `GET /buyer/statement` serves (apps/api/src/buyer/buyer.controller.ts:248-255 -> `this.customersService.getStatementForOperator(ctx.customerId)`), i.e. this method is buyer-facing, not operator-only.

Before this change both halves of the wallet came from ONE read: `creditNote.findMany({ where: { customerId }, orderBy: createdAt desc, take: 50 })`. `availableCredit` summed that 50-row page and `transactions` listed the same 50 rows, so the dollar value and the credit rows always agreed (both wrong the same way — that is B110).

After this change they are two different populations:
- `openCreditNotes` (line 976-979 area, `where: { customerId, status: { not: "VOID" } }`, NO take) -> `availableCredit` at line 1034.
- `ledgerCreditNotesRaw` (`take: LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP + 1` = 51, `orderBy: createdAt desc`, line 979) -> `ledgerCreditNotes` (line 1009) -> the `transactions` array.

Three existing consumers read the credits out of `transactions`, not out of `availableCredit`:
- apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/finances/page.tsx:106-108 — `activeCredits = (statement?.transactions ?? []).filter(t => t.type === "CREDIT_NOTE" && t.runningBalance > 0.001).slice(0,6)`; rendered as the tile sub-label at :182 (`${activeCredits.length} active` / "None available") and as the credit LIST at :219-226.
- apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/payments/page.tsx:145-147 and :254 — same derivation, same sub-label.
- apps/mobile/app/(customer)/payments.tsx:66 — `activeCreditRows(statement?.transactions)`.

Failure scenario: a buyer has 60 credit notes. The 50 newest are fully consumed (`amount - amountUsed == 0`); ten older ones still hold $50 each. After this change `availableCredit` = $500 (uncapped read sees the ten old ones), while `transactions` holds only the newest 50 credit notes, every one of which has `runningBalance` 0. The web buyer portal then renders the wallet tile as "$500.00" with the sub-label "None available", and the `activeCredits.length > 0 &&` guard at finances/page.tsx:219 suppresses the credit list entirely — the buyer is told they hold $500 of store credit and simultaneously that they have none, with no row to identify. The mobile screen behaves the same way. The `transactionsTruncated` flag that this change added exactly to disclose a capped ledger is wired only into the OPERATOR surfaces (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx LedgerTruncationNote, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/customers/[id]/statement.tsx); the buyer surfaces got the field in their types (packages/types/api/buyer.ts `BuyerStatement.transactionsTruncated`) but no consumer.

The new code comment at customers.service.ts:966-971 asserts "the LEDGER caps below are for the transactions DISPLAY only — the money figures ... are computed from the separate, uncapped OPEN-set reads". That invariant is false across the package boundary: three call sites derive a money-bearing list (which credits the buyer can spend) from the capped array.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either return the open credit-note rows as their own field on the statement (e.g. `activeCredits`) and repoint finances/page.tsx:106, payments/page.tsx:145 and mobile payments.tsx:66 at it, or keep the credit-note ledger read uncapped so the list and `availableCredit` stay one population. If neither, wire `transactionsTruncated` into the buyer surfaces so the count is at least labelled partial.
remainingFindings.decision: The evidence shows a real split: availableCredit now sums an uncapped non-VOID read while the buyer-facing credit rows and their count still come from the 51-row ledger page, and nothing labels the ledger as partial (the truncation flag has no consumer and its predicate is already flagged wrong). It is a visible tile-vs-rows contradiction on a buyer surface, but it is a consequence of the accepted uncapped-totals/capped-ledger design rather than a wrong dollar figure, so minor and largely absorbed by the open no-consumer/wrong-predicate findings.

remainingFindings.summary: The customer Statement tab's four-tile header now mixes bases: "Invoiced Amount" and "Amount Received" are still summed from the 100-row capped `transactions` ledger while "Balance Due" was repointed at the newly uncapped, DRAFT-excluding `outstandingAmount`, so the three tiles no longer reconcile.
remainingFindings.detail:
The tiles are built at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx:3818-3863:
- :3828 "Invoiced Amount" = `statement.transactions.filter(tx => tx.type === "INVOICE").reduce((s,tx) => s + Math.abs(tx.amount), 0)`
- :3839 "Amount Received" = that figure minus `Σ |tx.runningBalance|` over the same INVOICE rows (the comment says explicitly "received = invoiced − still-owed on the listed rows")
- :3854 "Balance Due" = `statement?.outstandingAmount`

Before this change all three came from ONE population: `invoice.findMany({ where: { customerId }, orderBy: createdAt desc, take: 100 })` — `outstandingAmount` was reduced from exactly the rows that became `transactions`, so `Invoiced − Received = Balance Due` held by construction over those 100 rows.

After this change (apps/api/src/customers/customers.service.ts:955-1030) `outstandingAmount` comes from `openInvoices` — an uncapped read with `status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED }` (PAID/VOID/WRITTEN_OFF/DRAFT excluded) — while `transactions` is still built from `ledgerInvoices`, the newest 100 rows of ALL statuses.

Failure scenario: a customer with 250 invoices of which 120 are open, totalling $60,000 outstanding; the 100 newest invoices total $40,000 invoiced with $30,000 still owed on them. The Statement tab now renders Opening Balance $0.00 / Invoiced Amount $40,000.00 / Amount Received $10,000.00 / Balance Due $60,000.00 — arithmetic an operator (or the customer they print this statement for) cannot reconcile: 0 + 40,000 − 10,000 = 30,000, not 60,000. Two further axes push the same way: the ledger includes DRAFT invoices (so "Invoiced Amount" counts totals "Balance Due" deliberately excludes), and `runningBalance` per row switched to the CONFIRMED (`sumConfirmed`) basis while nothing else in the tile row did.

The `LedgerTruncationNote` added at :3873 sits BELOW this tile row and says only that the transaction LIST is partial; it does not tell the reader that three of the four numbers above it are computed from that partial list while the fourth is not.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Feed the tile row from the same population as Balance Due — either have the API return invoiced/received totals alongside `outstandingAmount` (computed over the same uncapped open set), or move the truncation note above the tile row and label the two ledger-derived tiles as covering the listed transactions only.
remainingFindings.decision: Before the change the three Statement-tab tiles were reduced from one 100-row population so Invoiced − Received = Balance Due held by construction; now Balance Due is the uncapped DRAFT-excluding outstandingAmount while the other two are still summed off the capped ledger rows, so an operator sees three money tiles that no longer add up. That is a new, user-visible arithmetic contradiction introduced by this change on a money screen.

remainingFindings.summary: The customer Invoices-tab summary bar now mixes a whole-tenant figure with two chip-scoped ones: "Outstanding" reads the statement while "Overdue" and "Total Invoices" are still counted off the currently-filtered, 50-row `invoicesData` page.
remainingFindings.detail:
apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx:3531-3568. `invoicesData` is `useInvoices({ customerId, status: invoiceFilter === "paid" ? "PAID" : invoiceFilter === "void" ? "VOID" : undefined, limit: 50 })` (declared at :1957-1961) — it re-fetches whenever the operator clicks the All / Outstanding / Paid / Void chips at :3583-3600. `overdueCount` (:3539) and "Total Invoices" (:3568, `invoicesData?.meta?.total`) therefore track the active chip, while `outstandingTotal` (:3540) is now `statement?.outstandingAmount`, which never varies with the chip.

Before this change all three cards were derived from the same `invoicesData` response, so they moved together.

Failure scenario: a customer with $12,400 open and 3 VOID invoices. The operator clicks the "Void" chip. The card row then reads "Outstanding $12,400.00 · Overdue 0 invoices · Total Invoices 3" — the header claims the customer has three invoices while showing the full open balance beside it. The "Paid" chip produces the same shape.

Secondary: `statement` is a separate query (`useCustomerStatement`, :1949) with no loading state consumed here, so while it is in flight the Outstanding card renders `$0.00` in success styling (`text-success`, :3546) rather than a skeleton — previously it was derived from data the tab had already loaded.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either scope the whole card row to the statement (drive Overdue/Total from server-side figures too) or leave a chip-independent label on the Outstanding card so it does not read as a property of the filtered set.
remainingFindings.decision: The Outstanding card was repointed at the statement (whole-customer, chip-independent) while Overdue and Total Invoices still track the active status chip and the 50-row page, so the Void chip can read 'Outstanding $12,400 · Total Invoices 3'. A real mixed-scope header, but a labelling inconsistency rather than a wrong amount.

remainingFindings.summary: The orders CSV export was rewritten to send its filters to the server instead of filtering client-side, but `productId` — a filter that IS applied to the on-screen list — was not added to the export params, so exporting with a product chip active produces a CSV of every order.
remainingFindings.detail:
The B144 fix's stated purpose is that a filter must reach the server rather than be applied to whatever page the client happens to hold. The on-screen query at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/orders/page.tsx:341-350 sends `status`, `urgent`, `deliveryDateFrom`, `deliveryDateTo`, `productId: productIdFilter || undefined`, `fulfillPath`, `search`, `page`, `limit`. `handleExport` (:373-400) sends `status`, `urgent`, `deliveryDateFrom`, `deliveryDateTo`, `fulfillPath`, `search`, `page: 1`, `limit: 1000` — no `productId`. This hunk was edited by this change (the `search` line at :397 was added and the client-side `.filter()` over `payload.data` was deleted), so the param list was under the author's hand. Failure scenario: the operator opens `/orders?productId=

` (the "which orders had this item?" chip, whose label is rendered from `useProduct(productIdFilter)` at :147), sees 12 matching orders, clicks Export. The request goes out without `productId`, the API returns the first 1000 orders for the tenant, and `downloadCsv` writes all of them — the CSV silently contains orders that do not contain the product, and previously the deleted client-side filter did not catch this either (it only matched on business name / order number). The operator's on-screen count and their CSV row count disagree by three orders of magnitude. Separately, `EXPORT_LIMIT = 1000` is now exactly `MAX_LIST_LIMIT`, so with `@Max(MAX_LIST_LIMIT)` newly added to `ListOrdersDto.limit` (apps/api/src/orders/dto/list-orders.dto.ts:28) the export can no longer be widened past 1000 without a DTO change, and a tenant with more than 1000 matching orders gets a silently truncated CSV with no warning — the same silent-truncation class F16 exists to remove.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add `productId: productIdFilter || undefined` to the handleExport params so the export matches the on-screen query exactly.
remainingFindings.decision: The B144 hunk was rewritten so export filters travel to the server, yet productId — which the on-screen query does send — was left out of the export params, so a product-filtered view exports every order. The evidence does not prove the deleted client-side filter previously honoured productId, so it may be pre-existing, but it is in the edited hunk and squarely within the bug's stated purpose.

remainingFindings.summary: `getKpiSummary` buckets purely by due date and drops the client memo's `status === "OVERDUE"` disjunct, but the Overdue tile it feeds still filters the list by `status=OVERDUE` on click, so the tile's value and the list it opens can disagree.
remainingFindings.detail:
Server bucketing: apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3050-3055 — `if (dueDateIso == null) continue; if (dueDateIso < today) overdue += balance; else if (dueDateIso === today) dueToday += balance; else if (dueDateIso <= cutoff) dueIn30 += balance;`. The memo this replaces (deleted at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:225-320) read `if (inv.status === "OVERDUE" || (due && due < today && openForCollection)) overdue += balance;` — status OR date.

The tile is still a filter button: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:284-291 renders `label: "Overdue", value: fmt(kpis.overdue)` with `onClick: () => onFilter(activeFilter === "OVERDUE" ? "" : "OVERDUE")`, which sets `statusFilter` and is sent to `findAll` as `status`, matching the literal `InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE` column (invoices.service.ts:2820-2821).

The divergent state is reachable: `update(id, dto)` at apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3156 writes `...(dto.dueDate && { dueDate: new Date(dto.dueDate) })` (:3360) and never calls `recomputeStatus` — unlike `updateInvoiceTerms`, which does (:~3480, `const newStatus = this.recomputeStatus(totalPaid, Number(inv.total), newDueDate, inv.status)`). So an invoice already stamped OVERDUE by the nightly job, whose due date is then pushed forward through the generic invoice update, keeps `status = OVERDUE` with a future `dueDate`.

Failure scenario: INV-1, balance $5,000, status OVERDUE, dueDate moved to today+10 via a plain invoice edit; it is the tenant's only past-due row. The Overdue tile now shows $0.00 (INV-1 is bucketed into dueIn30 instead); the operator clicks it and the list returns INV-1 with $5,000 due. The behaviour is deliberately pinned by the new T6 case `inv-status-overdue`, so the test suite will not surface it — the defect is that the pinned semantics break the tile's own click target.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either restore the `status === OVERDUE` disjunct in the server bucketing, or change the Overdue tile's onClick to the derived `isOverdue` filter that findAll already implements (status in SENT/VIEWED/PARTIAL/OVERDUE and dueDate < now) so value and filter share one definition.
remainingFindings.decision: The server buckets Overdue by dueDate only while the tile's click still filters the list by status=OVERDUE, and the evidence shows the status/date divergence is reachable via update(); the tile value and the list it opens can disagree. Kept as minor because the date-only bucketing may be the cause-ruling's chosen definition — the fixer must check section 2 before treating it as a defect rather than re-adding the disjunct.

remainingFindings.summary: `getKpiSummary` replaces a 999-row client cap with an unbounded server `findMany` that materializes every open invoice plus every one of their payment rows in Node on each `/invoices` load, while the sibling figure in the same `Promise.all` is a proper SQL aggregate.
remainingFindings.detail:
apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3001-3009: `this.prisma.forTenant().invoice.findMany({ where: { status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED }, ...(customerId ? { customerId } : {}) }, select: { total: true, dueDate: true, payments: { select: { amount: true, status: true } } } })` — no `take`, no pagination, and a nested relation select so Prisma issues a second query with an `IN (...)` list of every open invoice id. The five money figures are then reduced in JS at :3044-3056.

The `avgDays` leg of the same `Promise.all` (:3013-3027) is a single `$queryRaw` `AVG(...)` — so the aggregate-in-SQL option was available and used for one of the six tiles and not the other five.

Failure scenario: an established tenant carrying 40,000 open invoices with an average of 2 payment rows each. Every operator opening `/invoices` (and every React Query refetch after any invoice mutation invalidates the `["invoices"]` key) pulls 40,000 invoice rows plus ~80,000 payment rows into the API process and reduces them per request. This is the hot path of the app's busiest page, on the same dyno that serves everything else; the bug being fixed (B12) was precisely that this set is bigger than a page.

This is a scale/latency risk rather than a wrong number — it is called out because the fix's own premise is "the open set is bigger than any cap", and it is the one place in the diff where that premise is answered by removing the cap rather than by aggregating.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Replace the findMany+reduce with a grouped SQL aggregate (SUM over the open set, bucketed by dueDate against the caller's `today`, netting CONFIRMED payments) alongside the avgDays query, or accept the read with an explicit ceiling + documented tenant-size bound.
remainingFindings.decision: The KPI read is an unbounded findMany with a nested payments select reduced in JS, on every /invoices load and every React Query invalidation, while the sibling avgDays leg proves a SQL aggregate was available. Not a wrong-output defect, but a real scaling regression versus the 999-row cap it replaced for the tenants B12 was meant to serve.

remainingFindings.summary: `awaitingConfirmationCount` counts DRAFT payments across every invoice status, including invoices the caller is not allowed to see — a CUSTOMER's tile can be non-zero while every invoice they can open has no draft payment.
remainingFindings.detail:
apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:3010-3012: `this.prisma.forTenant().invoicePayment.count({ where: { status: "DRAFT", ...(customerId ? { invoice: { customerId } } : {}) } })`. There is no invoice-status restriction — unlike the sibling read three lines above, which narrows to `KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED`.

`findAll` explicitly hides DRAFT invoices from buyers (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:2823-2836: "Buyers must not see DRAFT invoices (not yet issued to them)"), and the KPI route is now open to `UserRole.CUSTOMER` (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.controller.ts:88-92), with the tile rendered unconditionally on the invoices page (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/page.tsx:577, no `isCustomer` guard, unlike :532/:814/:859).

Failure scenario: an operator records two unconfirmed (DRAFT) payments against a DRAFT invoice for buyer B. Buyer B opens `/invoices`: the list shows no DRAFT invoice at all (correctly), but the "Awaiting Confirmation" tile reads 2 with the hint "Draft payments not yet counted as paid" (page.tsx:296-315). The tile has no onClick, so the buyer has no row to reconcile it against — and its non-zero value discloses the existence of an invoice deliberately withheld from them. The same unscoped population applies to operators: the count spans payments on VOID and WRITTEN_OFF invoices, which every other tile in the bar excludes.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Narrow the count's `where` to the same open-invoice population the other tiles use (`invoice: { status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED }, ...(customerId ? { customerId } : {}) }`), so the tile counts only payments on invoices the caller can actually open.
remainingFindings.decision: awaitingConfirmationCount has no invoice-status restriction, so DRAFT payments on DRAFT invoices — which findAll deliberately hides from buyers — inflate a tile now served to CUSTOMER role and rendered unguarded; a buyer can see a non-zero count with no matching invoice. Real and a small information leak, distinct from the open CUSTOMER-403 blocker on the same route.

remainingFindings.summary: The REG-B110 e2e test — the only surviving web-side proof of B110 after T9 was withdrawn — asserts $0.00 against $0.00 and therefore passes identically on the buggy and the fixed build.
remainingFindings.detail:
The test provisions its own fixture: one customer, then one invoice via `POST /api/v1/invoices` (37-list-caps.spec.ts:307-315, `items: [{ description: "E2E B110 line", qty: 1, unitPrice: 250 }]`). `InvoicesService.create` hardcodes `status: InvoiceStatus.DRAFT` (apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:507) and the DTO carries no status field, so the fixture invoice is always DRAFT and is never sent.

On the FIXED build, `getStatementForOperator` reads its open set as `where: { customerId, status: { notIn: KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED } }` (customers.service.ts:~932) and `KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED` now includes `DRAFT` (invoice-status-sets.ts:36-41). So the DRAFT fixture is excluded and `statement.outstandingAmount === 0`. The spec then sets `const expected = fmtMoney(statement.outstandingAmount)` (line 331) = "$0.00" and asserts both the Profile-tab "Open Balance" tile and the Invoices-tab "Outstanding" card equal it.

On the PRE-FIX build the same two reads are also 0: the Profile tile already read `fmt(statement?.outstandingAmount ?? 0)` (customers/[id]/page.tsx:2390-2391) and the old Invoices-tab card reduced `allInvoices.filter(inv => ["SENT","VIEWED","PARTIAL","OVERDUE"].includes(inv.status))` — which also excludes DRAFT — over a single-invoice customer. Both render "$0.00", the assertion passes, and the test reports green against the defect it names.

The defect B110's web half is about is a page-scoped client reduce diverging from the whole-set server figure. Reproducing it needs (a) a non-DRAFT (sent) invoice so `outstandingAmount` is non-zero at all, and (b) more open invoices for that customer than one page of the Invoices tab, so the client reduce undercounts. The fixture has neither: one DRAFT invoice. With T9 explicitly withdrawn (build-plan.md P4, bug-test-plan.md T9), this is the only test anywhere covering the web leg of REG-B110, so reverting P4's `outstandingTotal = statement?.outstandingAmount ?? 0` change (customers/[id]/page.tsx:3540) back to the client-side reduce leaves the whole suite green.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Make the fixture non-vacuous: send the invoice (POST /invoices/:id/send, or create it via an order path that issues it) so outstandingAmount is non-zero, and create more open invoices for the fixture customer than one page of the Invoices tab renders, so the pre-fix client-side reduce genuinely disagrees with the statement figure. Then assert both tiles equal the API's own outstandingAmount.
remainingFindings.decision: The fixture is a single DRAFT invoice (create() hardcodes DRAFT, the DTO has no status), so the statement's open set excludes it and outstandingAmount is 0 on both builds; and even if DRAFT were counted, a one-invoice fixture cannot distinguish a capped read from an uncapped one, so the only surviving web-side REG-B110 proof cannot fail on the bug it claims to pin. A fixer must confirm which exclusion set the statement now uses, but the test is tautological under either.

remainingFindings.summary: The buyer wallet tile now reads the uncapped `availableCredit` while the credit rows beside it still come from the 50-row capped ledger, so the tile and its own "N active" sub-label can contradict each other — and `transactionsTruncated`, the flag added to disclose exactly this, is read on no buyer surface at all.
remainingFindings.detail:
This is the mobile half the earlier reader did not trace. `GET /buyer/statement` is served by `getStatementForOperator` (apps/api/src/buyer/buyer.controller.ts:248-255), the same method P3 changed, so the mobile customer app and the web buyer portal both inherit the new split.

After the change the two credit reads are no longer the same rows (customers.service.ts, getStatementForOperator):
- `openCreditNotes`: `where: { customerId, status: { not: "VOID" } }`, NO `take` — this feeds `availableCredit` (line ~1034).
- `ledgerCreditNotesRaw`: `where: { customerId }` (ALL statuses, VOID and expired included), `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }`, `take: LEDGER_CREDIT_NOTE_CAP + 1` = 51, sliced to 50 — this feeds the `transactions` array.

Before the change both figures came from ONE read (`where: { customerId }, orderBy createdAt desc, take: 50`), so the tile and the rows always agreed (both under-reported together). They can now disagree.

Mobile consumer, apps/mobile/app/(customer)/payments.tsx:
- line 52 `const { data: statement } = useBuyerStatement();`
- line 66 `const credits = activeCreditRows(statement?.transactions);` — apps/mobile/lib/buyer-payments-logic.ts:34-36 filters `t.type === "CREDIT_NOTE" && t.runningBalance > 0.001` over the capped ledger rows.
- lines 112-116 render `Tile label="Store credit" value={money(statement?.availableCredit)} sub={credits.length > 0 ? `${credits.length} active` : "None available"}`.
- line 126 gates the whole "Active credits" card on `credits.length > 0`.

Failure scenario: a buyer has 3 open credit notes worth $50 each issued in January, and 55 credit notes issued since then that are fully used or VOID (`amount - amountUsed == 0`, so `runningBalance` is 0 on those rows). The uncapped `openCreditNotes` read still sums the 3 open ones → `availableCredit = 150`. The ledger read takes the 51 newest by `createdAt` — all of them used/VOID — and slices to 50, so no open note appears in `transactions`. `activeCreditRows` returns `[]`. The screen renders "Store credit $150.00 / None available" and omits the "Active credits" card entirely: the buyer is told they hold $150 of store credit and simultaneously that none is available, with no way to see which notes it is. Pre-change the tile would have read $0.00 — also wrong, but self-consistent, and B110's stated goal was the uncapped figure plus a labelled partial view.

The labelled-partial-view half never reaches this screen. `transactionsTruncated` IS emitted by the API and IS declared on the shared buyer type (packages/types/api/buyer.ts:104-105, non-optional `boolean`), and in the 55-used-note case above it is `true` (51 > 50). But a repo-wide grep for `transactionsTruncated` across apps/web and apps/mobile returns only: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/{ledger-truncation-note.tsx,page.tsx:3874}, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/customers/[id]/statement.tsx:138, plus the type declarations. Neither apps/mobile/app/(customer)/payments.tsx, nor apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/payments/page.tsx:145,253 (identical `activeCredits` filter + `fmt(statement?.availableCredit)` StatCard with the same "N active"/"None available" sub-label), nor apps/web/app/buyer/portal/[seller]/finances/page.tsx:106,181 reads it. Only the two OPERATOR statement surfaces disclose truncation; every BUYER-facing surface still presents the capped ledger as complete beside an uncapped total.

Separately answering the decider's third question: no mobile screen sums ledger rows into a money figure. `activeCreditRows` filters and never sums (buyer-payments-logic.ts header states this explicitly), the mobile operator statement screen renders `fmtMoney(Math.abs(t.runningBalance))` per row only, and the operator customer hub (apps/mobile/app/(operator)/customers/[id].tsx:222-249) reads server tiles verbatim. The contradiction is tile-vs-row-set, not tile-vs-recomputed-sum.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide the buyer disclosure: either render a truncation line on the buyer payments/finances surfaces (web + mobile) when `statement.transactionsTruncated` is true — the same shape as LedgerTruncationNote / the mobile operator statement line — or stop deriving the credit LIST from the capped all-status ledger and give the statement a dedicated uncapped open-credit-note array so the tile and its rows come from one source again.
remainingFindings.decision: GET /buyer/statement is served by the same getStatementForOperator P3 split, so the mobile wallet tile now reads the uncapped open-credit total while the rows and any 'N active' sub-label beside it come from a 50-row, all-status ledger — the two reads no longer share a basis and no mobile surface reads transactionsTruncated to label the partial view, which is the B110 design requirement. Fold into the already-open 'no consumer' fix rather than treating it as a separate defect.

remainingFindings.summary: The three sort-allowlist lookups this diff rewrites still use a bare index, so a prototype key (`sortBy=constructor`) resolves to an inherited value and reaches Prisma as a malformed orderBy (500) — while the sibling in this same diff, customers.service.ts, carries the Object.hasOwn guard that exists precisely for this.
remainingFindings.detail:
Pre-existing on master, but the batch rewrites these exact expressions for B169 and fixes the identical hazard one file over, so the sibling sweep stopped short.

The three rewritten sites:
- invoices.service.ts:2883-2888 (`findAll`): `const orderField = validSortFields[sortBy ?? ""] ?? "issueDate";` then `const orderBy: any = [{ [orderField]: orderDir }, { id: orderDir }];`
- invoices.service.ts:4464 (`listAllPayments`): `const orderBy = validSortFields[sortBy ?? ""] ?? [{ paidAt: "desc" }, { id: "desc" }];`
- invoices.service.ts:5595 (`exportPayments`): identical line.

`validSortFields` is a plain object literal, so its prototype chain is live. `??` only falls back on null/undefined, and an inherited value is neither. I confirmed the JS semantics with a Node probe this session:

  constructor -> function -> key: "function Object() { [native code] }"
  toString    -> function -> key: "function toString() { [native code] }"
  __proto__   -> object   -> key: "[object Object]"
  valueOf     -> function -> key: "function valueOf() { [native code] }"

Reachability: `ListInvoicesDto.sortBy` is a free `@IsOptional() @IsString() sortBy?: string` (apps/api/src/invoices/dto/list-invoices.dto.ts:29) with no `@IsIn`, and `listAllPayments`/`exportPayments` take `sortBy` straight off the query string as a raw `@Query("sortBy") sortBy?: string` (invoices.controller.ts:139-150). The route is open to OPERATOR and CUSTOMER (`@Get()` `@Roles(UserRole.OPERATOR, UserRole.CUSTOMER)`, controller class `@Roles(UserRole.OPERATOR)`).

Failure scenario: any authenticated operator or buyer issues `GET /api/v1/invoices?sortBy=constructor`. `validSortFields["constructor"]` resolves to `Object`, `??` does not fire, and Prisma receives `orderBy: [{ "function Object() { [native code] }": "desc" }, { id: "desc" }]` → PrismaClientValidationError. It is not an HttpException, so `SentryExceptionFilter` (extends `BaseExceptionFilter`, apps/api/src/common/sentry-exception.filter.ts:11) turns it into a 500 and reports it. `GET /api/v1/invoices/payments?sortBy=constructor` is worse: the whole `orderBy` becomes the `Object` function itself. `GET /api/v1/invoices/payments/export?sortBy=__proto__` hits the same line at 5595. Repeated calls are a cheap authenticated DoS plus Sentry flood.

The in-diff precedent and the exact fix shape are in the same commit: customers.service.ts:165-170 guards with `query.sortBy && Object.hasOwn(validSortFields, query.sortBy) ? validSortFields[query.sortBy] : undefined`, with the comment "Object.hasOwn (not a bare index) so prototype keys — __proto__, constructor, toString, valueOf… — can't resolve to a truthy inherited value and reach Prisma as a malformed orderBy (→ 500)", and its regression spec apps/api/src/customers/customers.security.spec.ts (F4-002) — which this diff also edits — enumerates exactly `["__proto__", "constructor", "toString", "valueOf", "hasOwnProperty"]`. No equivalent guard or spec exists for invoices.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Apply the customers.service.ts:165-170 shape to all three sites: gate the lookup on `Object.hasOwn(validSortFields, sortBy)` and fall back to the safe default otherwise, and add the F4-002-style `it.each(["__proto__","constructor","toString","valueOf","hasOwnProperty"])` coverage to invoices.service.spec.ts for findAll, listAllPayments and exportPayments.
remainingFindings.decision: validSortFields is a plain object literal, so sortBy=constructor resolves to Object.prototype.constructor (neither null nor undefined), survives the ?? fallback and reaches Prisma as a malformed orderBy key — a reproducible 500 on all three rewritten sites, while the customers.service.ts sibling in this same diff got the Object.hasOwn guard. Pre-existing, no money or data exposure, but the sweep stopped one file short.

remainingFindings.summary: getKpiSummary replaces a bounded 999-row client read with a completely unbounded server read of every open invoice plus every one of its payment rows — worst exactly on the tenants the bug is defined by.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide whether the four money buckets should be a single `$queryRaw` aggregate (SUM over `total - COALESCE(confirmed payments, 0)` bucketed by dueDate against the passed `today`/`today+30`), the way avgDays already is, instead of streaming the whole open set into Node. If the row-loop is kept deliberately, record the accepted ceiling.
remainingFindings.decision: The aggregate reads every open invoice plus its payment rows into Node with no take, so the cost scales with exactly the tenant size B12 is defined by; the figures are correct, so this is a performance/design concern (push the sums into SQL as avgDays already is), not a wrong-value defect.
